articleTitle: Design of Inspection Robot for Spherical Tank Based on Mecanum Wheel
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Traditional manual weld inspection of large spherical tank has high cost, low efficiency and high degree of danger. It is of great significance to design an automated weld flaw detection system. This paper designs a wheeled wall-climbing robot that can crawl on the outer wall of the spherical tank. The Mecanum wheeled trolley is used as a mobile platform for ultrasonic testing with ultrasonic testing equipment. Firstly, the key structure of the robot is introduced, and the independent suspension structure and spherical adjustment mechanism are designed. The reliability of magnetic adsorption was analyzed by static calculation, and the rationality of the structure was verified. The ultrasonic probe fixture is designed according to the ultrasonic flaw detection process. The defect size calculated according to the flaw detection principle. Through the experiment, the motion effect of the wall-climbing robot on the curved surface is analyzed, and the rationality and application value of the wall-detecting robot flaw detection scheme are verified.

articleTitle: UHF RFID Sensor Array for Bending stress assessment
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Ultra-high frequency (UHF) passive RFID sensing technology is a promising research direction in the field of combining structural health monitoring (SHM) and nondestructive testing (NDT) since the RFID passive tags meet the requirement of SHM with cheap, convenient and passive sensing. This paper investigates an UHF RFID sensor array to evaluate the deformation of a specimen due to bending stress. The interaction between tag arrays at different distances is discussed and the layout of tag sensor array is presented. In particular, the experiment of bending detection and the contrast validation of flexing sensor array are conducted. The relationship between the extracted eigenvalues from the RFID sensor array and bending deflection of the specimen is interpreted. Finally, the curvature of the sensor is compared with the characteristic value of tags in the array.

articleTitle: Comparison of Morphology Characterization for Regular Cracks with Multi-mode Total Focusing Method
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The multi-mode total focusing method (MTFM) is used for characterization of crack morphology, whose imaging quality is closely related to crack orientation. In this paper, the signal acquisition was performed using the 39° wedge and 16-element linear array probe with center frequency of 10 MHz. The morphology of regular cracks was characterized and compared by MTFM imaging in direct, half-skip and full-skip modes, respectively. The established simulation model was a 9.0 mm thickness aluminum plate containing a series of regular bottom cracks, whose lengths were all 2.0 mm and orientation angles were 0°, ±15°, ±35° and ±60°, respectively. The simulated results showed that direct, half-skip and full-skip modes were suitable for morphology characterization of regular cracks with orientation angles of 35°, 0° and -35°, respectively. The quantitative errors of crack lengths and orientation angles were no more than 0.22 mm and 0.8°, respectively. The measurement errors in experiment were within 0.28 mm and 0.9° for crack lengths and orientation angles, being in good agreement with simulated results. On the basis, the increment of element pitch is helpful for enlarging receiving area of ultrasonic beam and characterization range for crack morphology.

articleTitle: Bolt Detection of Key Component for High-speed Trains Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Safety inspection is a crucial task for high-speed trains. Conventional methods based on computer vision are insufficient in achieving this task by using template matching, the main reason is that it is difficult to extract image features, especially for the images of high-speed trains whose image edges are difficult to detect. In this paper, deep learning is introduced to key component detection. Deep learning method is not suitable when samples are rare, and as for our task, there are few abnormal samples because key component rarely become abnormal. However, abnormal detection can be transformed to the problem of bolt detection; it will be abnormal if bolts are lost. From this paper, Faster R-CNN and YOLO are adopted to detect bolts. Considering the purpose of the abnormal detection of bolts is to confirm whether the bolts are lost, and the location information of bolts contained in the extracted information of target detection is redundant. Therefore, a bolt number detection network based on ResNet is proposed to examine how many bolts on the key component. The number of bolts determine whether the bolts are lost. It shows that, this bolt number detection network achieves the task well.

articleTitle: Mechanism Hybrid EMAT and Eddy Current Sensing Detection for Surface and Internal Defects NDT
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Fast and efficient comprehensive inspection of oil and gas pipelines is a critical and challenging task. This paper proposes a novel mechanism hybrid non-destructive testing (NDT) method of Electromagnetic Acoustic Transducer (EMAT)and Pulsed Eddy Current Testing (PECT)for detecting surface and internal defects. This transceiver-integrated sensor simultaneously excites pulsed eddy current and ultrasonic waves and picks up composite signals. In particular, the ultrasound detects deep defects, and the eddy current detect surface defects. Numerical simulation and experiments have been carried out on the detection of hybrid defects. The feasibility, efficiency and reliability of the proposed method were verified.

articleTitle: A Research on Composite Nondestructive Testing Sensor of Boiler Water Wall Tubes
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a new composite NDT testing sensor for boiler water wall tubes defect detection is designed which using a combination of the electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) method, the magnetic flux leakage (MFL) method and the pulse eddy current testing (PECT) method. The purpose of the research is to make up for the limitation of the traditional single NDT method in terms of defect detection capability. Firstly, through analyzing the detection mechanism, establish the equivalent finite element of the composite detection sensor. Secondly, based on the numerical simulation, the working point for three different NDT methods and the structural parameters of composite detection sensor is determined. Thirdly, the experiment of the composite detection sensor is conducted cooperating with mechanical devices and testing equipment, and four types of defects on the water wall tubes are successfully identified. The experimental results proved the new hybrid NDT testing sensor can meet requirement of full-scale defects inspection for boiler water wall tubes.

articleTitle: Multimode Testing for Delamination Defects of Composite Materials Using Ultrasonic Guided Waves
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Delamination defects are one of the typical defects of composites materials. Due to the complex distributions of delamination defects, it is hard to use one mode of guided waves to detect delamination defects with different distributions. Thus a multimode testing method is highly demanded. Apply semi-analysis finite element (SAFE) method to calculate dispersion curves and wave structure. Several mode-frequency points from dispersion curves will be selected to do finite element simulation for delamination defects with different sizes but the same depth of composite materials plates. Then analyzes the sensitivity of guided waves for different delamination defects. The sensitive modes are selected to do defects testing experiments for composite materials plate with different delamination defects. The results show that using two or more mode-frequency points can detect out delamination defects with different sizes.

articleTitle: Visual Detection of AM Surface Defects Based on Laser Ultrasound Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) process is a kind of Additive Manufacturing (AM) method, which can process parts with arbitrary complex geometry. However, macro-defects will destroy the mechanical properties of metal materials manufactured by SLM. Laser ultrasound can excite broadband surface waves and realize non-contact nondestructive testing of surface defects. In this paper, 316L stainless steel samples are prepared by SLM process are used for laser ultrasonic detection. According to the diffraction phenomenon of surface wave at the defect, a laser ultrasonic B-scan detection platform is built. The B-scan images of different length defects on the sample surface are obtained, and the quantitative detection of surface defects is realized quickly. In order to further improve the signal-to-noise ratio and the accuracy of imaging detection, EEMD (Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition) denoising is applied to the collected ultrasonic signal, which improves the accuracy of imaging, makes the signal more stable and realizes the visual detection of surface length defects clearly and intuitively.

articleTitle: Probabilistic damage imaging of composite plates by air coupled Lamb waves
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Lamb wave of air coupled ultrasound can quickly detect the area of composite laminates. For the impact damage of quasi-isotropic carbon fiber composite laminates, a probabilistic damage imaging method independent of velocity is presented. Firstly, air-coupled ultrasonic transducers are used to scan in two orthogonal directions to obtain energy damage factors at different positions. Based on the probabilistic damage theory, the pixel points of each path are damaged probabilistically to determine the damage index of all paths. Finally, the damage indexes in each scanning direction are fused and the threshold value is introduced to realize the imaging of impact damage. The experimental results show that the damage factor combined with probabilistic damage imaging can better realize the localization and reconstruction of impact damage, and the imaging accuracy can be further improved by introducing the threshold value.

articleTitle: Ensemble Tensor Factorization for Background Subtraction in Thermography NDT
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper proposes an ensemble tensor factorization to extract defects signal of infrared thermography video. The proposed algorithm jointly models the soft weighted low rank and sparse tensor patterns as well as removing the ghosting. In particular, the weak defects information can be separated from the strong interference and the resolution contrast is significantly improved. A multi-layer ensemble iterative decomposition structure is conducted to further enhance the weak information. In order to verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, experimental studies have been carried out by applying electromagnetic thermal imaging system for cracks detection on samples with different geometry. The results of the experiments have indicated that the proposed method has significantly enhanced the contrast ratio between the defective regions and the non-defective regions.

articleTitle: Imaging-based NDT Methods for Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper reviews the non-destructive testing (NDT) methods used for electronic devices inspection. The C-mode scanning acoustic microscopy, X-ray, scanning electron microscope and infrared thermography are the most widely used NDT techniques in electronic devices testing and inspection. The typical testing scenarios are discussed along with merits and drawbacks for each technique. Newly developed NDT methods are introduced and the challenges/opportunities of NDT&E for electronic devices are provided.

articleTitle: Complexed Shape Micro Defects Inspection By High Sensitivity Flexible TRT Eddy Current Array
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: High sensitivity nondestructive testing on the complex geometric sample with near-surface micro defects is a critical research area in both scientific and industrial fields. This paper proposes a TRT (transmitting-receiving-transmitting)flexible eddy current sensing system in which incorporating double square windings excitation in parallel with multi-detectors for cracks inspection. Parameters of the probes are optimized through simulations to obtain satisfactory detection sensibilities of defects with different sizes and different orientation. The optimized new structure performs more capability and sensitivity to all presented near-surface micro defects. In addition, the simulation results can be used to cross-referenced and contrasted with the experimental investigations.

articleTitle: Bolt Axial Stress Detection and Calibration by Ultrasound Shear and Longitudinal Wave
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Based on the theory of acoustic elasticity, the relationship between ultrasonic body wave (shear wave and longitudinal wave) and stress is studied, and the technology of bolt axial stress detection is analyzed. In order to ensure the accuracy of the detection value and achieve traceability, the calibration technology of bolt axial stress ultrasonic body wave detection is studied. The temperature compensation algorithm and the precise measurement algorithm of acoustic time difference are designed by means of spontaneous selfcollection. The feasibility of the absolute calibration method of the axial force meter is verified by experiments. The ultrasonic shear and longitudinal wave testing and calibration system for bolt axial stress is established, which is applied to the axial stress testing of buildings, bridges and power stations.

articleTitle: Deep Adversarial Network for CFRP Thermal Imaging Debond Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a novel joint loss GAN is proposed in Thermography Nondestructive testing. The proposed joint loss function incorporates both the modified CGAN loss and the penalty loss where this strategy significantly improves performance of defect detection. The results show that the proposed method can better capture the defect features to improve the detection accuracy. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, experimental studies have been carried out for inner debond defects on both regular and irregular shaped CFRP specimens. A comparative analysis has been undertaken between the proposed method and the state-of-the-art deep semantic segmentation algorithms. It is being proved to be suitable for the end-to-end detection Thermography diagnosis system.

articleTitle: A method for improving calibration accuracy of Multi-robot Base Frame
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The calibration of the relative positional relationship between the base frame of multiple robots is the basis of multi-robot collaborative work. Therefore, it is necessary to accurately measure the relative positional relationship. The calibration method based on the robot itself has the advantages of simple operation and low cost, but the teaching accuracy is difficult to be guaranteed and the calibration accuracy is low. The four- point calibration method proposed in this paper was based on the calibration method of the robot itself. Adopted the principle of homogenization error to improve the calibration accuracy. The ultrasonic scanning experiment proves that the method can reduce the calibration error to 1mm and can effectively improve the accuracy of automated ultrasonic testing.

articleTitle: Novel Yoke Structured Electromagnetic Thermography for Inspection of Natural Fatigue Cracks
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Nondestructive detection of small fatigue cracks is a significative and challenging task in evaluating the properties of material. This paper proposes a novel yoke structured eddy current pulsed thermography (ECPT) system for micro fatigue cracks inspection on irregularly shaped metallic materials. The proposed detection model provides a region of interest with a relatively uniform magnetic field. The detectability and thermal contrast of omnidirectional micro fatigue cracks are enhanced remarkably. In addition, the configuration has advantages of dramatically increasing portability and efficiency for detecting complex workpiece since the detection is completely in the open view of the infrared camera. Finally, experimental studies have been conducted on natural fatigue cracks in order to validate the reliability and efficiency of the proposed sensing structure.

articleTitle: Total Focusing Algorithm of Double Layer Media Based on Iterative Process
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to ensure the position of the refraction point of the double-layer medium in the full-focus imaging algorithm when in immersion test, this paper carries out the time of flight trajectory of the research, put forward by the method of extreme points to look for refraction and put forward the ray intersection method as a Newton iterative method of the initial test point. The theory of this method is deduced to satisfy Snell's law of refraction and Fermat principle. A 64 array full matrix acquisition and full focus imaging algorithm is used to verify the computational efficiency and imaging quality of the extreme iteration method (EIM). The results show that the imaging speed of the EIM is about 50 times faster than that of the analytical solution model.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of Ultrasonic FMC/TFM on Real Fatigue Cracks
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Using ultrasonic arrays to detect and evaluate Surface Breaking Cracks (SBCs) is important in the Non-destructive Evaluation (NDE) field. It can provide early stage detection of failure and useful information for component integrity evaluation. The Full Matrix Capture (FMC) can achieve the maxim data from an ultrasonic array and the Total Focusing Method (TFM) is used for imaging. As a powerful method for crack characterisation, machined slots are usually used to examine and assess FMC/TFM methodology. In this paper, real SBCs are fabricated in 3-point bending specimens following ASTM standard E1820 and used to examine the performance of this ultrasonic imaging method. This approach is shown to work well in imaging and sizing of real fatigue cracks.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Ultrasonic Testing of TC4 Titanium Alloy by Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Research about ultrasonic testing was carried out for different processing states (hot isostatic and heat treated) of the additive manufacturing TC4 titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) by electron beam rapid manufacturing technique. Firstly, the longitudinal wave velocity and attenuation coefficient of the parts in these two processing states were measured by the contact longitudinal wave reflection method. Then, the signal-to-noise ratio of the φ0.8mm flat bottom hole defect buried depth 20-50mm was studied by using the water immersion ultrasonic method, the ultrasonic testing parameters and detection methods for different processes were analyzed. The results show that for the same processing state, the longitudinal wave velocity parallel to the deposition direction is significantly higher than that perpendicular to the deposition direction, and the attenuation coefficient is smaller than that perpendicular to the deposition direction; For the situation of different processing states, compared with the hot isostatic state , the longitudinal wave velocity of the material in heat treatment state is obviously reduced, and the attenuation coefficient is relatively close. For defects with buried depth of not more than 40 mm, it's more effective to detect the defects in the direction perpendicular to the deposition direction, within the heat treatment state, the signal-to-noise ratio is relatively high; When the buried depth is greater than 40mm, the signal-to-noise ratio is significantly reduced, and the detection result can be optimized by setting correct DAC curve.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic microscopy method for coating and interface bonding quality detection
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper describes methods for non-destructive testing of the bonding quality of coatings and interfaces by an ultrasonic microscopy system. Based on previous studies, the reflection and transmission echoes of ultrasonic waves at the coating/matrix and other forms of multi-layer interfaces were analyzed, and the relationship between the echo signals and bonding quality of the interfaces was derived. The ultrasonic microscopy was used for non-destructive testing. In experiments, coating specimens, a titanium alloy superconducting device and the laminated Silicon wafers were tested and bonding qualities of which were obtained.

articleTitle: Laser line generation for optimized interaction with hidden defects in active thermography
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, an active thermal imaging technique using a laser as an excitation source is used to detect aluminum specimens containing artificial defects. The presence of defects in the local excitation of the laser can produce better edge effects, using different laser excitation methods to improve edge effects. In the experiment, the laser scanning method is designed according to the characteristics of artificial defects, and the experimental data is analyzed. PPT and Sobel filtering are used to further data processing to obtain clearer defect edges and detect the detailed features of the defects. The study found that the detection effect is the best when the laser power and pulse width are large.

articleTitle: Effect of Temperature on Nonlinearity of Ultrasonic Waves in Metallic Solids
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The effect of temperature on the nonlinearity of ultrasonic waves propagating in metallic solids was studied experimentally. The metal block and rail were used as experimental objects respectively. The nonlinear parameters of ultrasonic bulk waves propagating in a metal block and ultrasonic guided waves propagating in a rail were measured during the temperature change process. The experimental results indicate that temperature has obvious influence on the nonlinearity of ultrasonic bulk waves or guided waves propagating in metallic solids. The ultrasonic nonlinear parameter of metallic solids increases with the increase of temperature and decreases with the decrease of temperature, which suggesting that it is necessary to compensate the effect of temperature when using nonlinear ultrasonic technology to detect relevant structures.

articleTitle: Research on Excitation Layout of Ring Flexible Eddy Current Array Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Ring flexible eddy current array sensor is a kind of sensor used for crack monitoring at bolt hole edge, and the layout of the excitation coil has a certain influence on the sensitivity of the crack detection of the sensor. In this paper, the effects of two different layout modes, co-directional excitation and reverse excitation on the sensitivity of crack monitoring are studied. The simulation model of the sensor under the two different layout modes of the co-directional excitation and reverse excitation was established by the COMSOL software. The sensitivity of the crack detection of the sensor under two layout modes was analyzed, and then the sensors of two layout modes were manufactured. The correctness of simulation results was studied through experiment. The results show that the crack monitoring sensitivity of the co-directional excitation layout is significantly higher than that of the reverse excitation layout. In the simulation results, the lowest sensitivity under the codirectional excitation layout is about 12 times of the highest sensitivity under the reverse excitation layout. In the experiment results, the lowest sensitivity under the co-excitation layout is about 3.5 times of the highest sensitivity under the reverse excitation layout. The research results provide an important way to improve the sensitivity of the sensor for crack monitoring.

articleTitle: Exposed Corrosion Progression Characterisation Using Pulsed Eddy Current Sensing and Laser Profilometry
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The progression characterisation of exposed atmospheric corrosion on metal substrates is a major problem in the field of corrosion science and Non-destructive Evaluation (NDE). A pulsed eddy current (PEC) sensing system and a laser profilometry have been used to characterise the corrosion on the mild steel plate. These mild steel (S275) samples have been exposed to marine environment (exposure time from 1 month to 10 months). Four features have been utilized to characterise conductivity, permeability, roughness and thickness variation in the corrosion layer. The relationship between these features and corrosion exposed time has been derived which is useful for corrosion progression measurement, early stage corrosion monitoring and prediction in industrial fields such as the marine industry.

articleTitle: A Locating Algorithm of Train Wheel Flaws in Ultrasonic Images Based on Cross-Correlation and Wavelet Packet Denoising
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The ultrasonic phased array inspection technology has been applied to the train wheels detection. Because of the environment and characteristics of ultrasonic phased array testing, many testing images are interfered by serious noise and clutter interference, so it is difficult to identify all the flaws and will take inspector a long time. This paper presents an automatic locating algorithm of train wheel flaws in ultrasonic images based on cross-correlation and Wavelet packet denoising. Firstly, preprocessing is acted on the images, including de-noising and adaptive threshold processing. Secondly, as the echo images of web hole have periodic feature in spatial domain, image cross-correlation theory is used for extracting the period, then the echo images of web hole is removed from the B-scan images. Finally, another threshold is needed to remove small bright areas, and then the location information of flaws is obtained. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively locate the flaws, and the average locating accuracy is higher than 96%.

articleTitle: Phased-Array Laser Ultrasonic Testing with Sparse Total Focusing Imaging Method
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to further improve the detectability of laser ultrasonic testing method for internal defects of materials, this paper studies a new phased array laser ultrasonic detection and imaging method based on the full matrix capture technology and total focusing method. Based on the finite element method, a numerical model of full matrix laser ultrasonic detection and signal sampling is developed to acquire the signal data of full matrix laser ultrasonic testing, and then the corresponding program of the total focusing method algorithm is developed to realize the visual imaging detection of different defects in the specimen based on the total focusing method. Subsequently, in order to improve the efficiency of laser ultrasonic testing with full matrix phased array, a full matrix laser ultrasonic testing method with sparse array is proposed, and a signal reproduction method based on sparse array is developed to expand sparse array to dense array signal, thus achieving high quality imaging of internal defects, and effectively improving the detection efficiency of this method.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic microscopy system performance calibration technology
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This article describes how to calibrate and compensate the performance of an ultrasonic microscopy system. Starting from the ultrasonic characteristics and ultrasonic transducers, the factors affecting the detection performance of the ultrasonic microscopy system were analyzed, and the calibration methods for the lateral and vertical detection dimensional accuracy were proposed respectively. The compensation method of detection performance was studied by learning the source of error. In the experiments, lateral and vertical dimension detection calibration blocks were fabricated and tested, and the calibration results were obtained.

articleTitle: Effect of Time Resolution on Measuring Newtonian Fluid Viscosity by the Phase of Reflected Shear Wave
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Ultrasonic is an important method to study the viscoelastic properties of liquid at high frequency. Relationship between the viscosity and phase change between incident wave and reflected wave from solid-fluid interface was obtained by acoustic shear impedance model. High resolution time measurement is the key to determine the phase changes of Newtonian fluid which has decoupled relation between amplitude and phase of the reflection coefficient. Various parameters affecting phase difference including the material properties of the solid, the operating frequency and the resolution were discussed in this paper, then the time scales were analyzed theoretically for Newtonian fluid/Plexiglas combination. The results shown that time error of a few tenths of nanosecond can make large deviation in viscosity for lower viscosity products.

articleTitle: Research on Phased Array Detection Technology of Inserted fillet weld
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Influences of irregular welding area and curvature change of ultrasonic reflection position in insertion fillet weld make it impossible to distinguish defect wave from internal reflection wave effectively in conventional ultrasonic testing, which leads to missed detection and inaccurate location of defects. Ultrasound phased array can control the focus and deflection of sound beam by controlling the excitation time of each piezoelectric chip in phased array, so as to improve the detection efficiency and accuracy. The parameters of probe and scanning method of phased array are determined by simulation in this paper, and an ultrasonic phased array detection system with scanning device is set up to detect the embedded defects in the insertion fillet weld.. The test results verify the efficiency and accuracy of the ultrasonic phased array detection for such welds, which provides an effective method for defect detection of inserted fillet weld.

articleTitle: The Simulation of SH Guided Wave at Weld by Peridynamics Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: SH guided wave detection technology is a new type of weld inspection technology. In order to solve non derivable problem of the SH guided wave at the defects, an integral equation of SH guided wave in the weld seam is established based on the peridynamics theory. This integral equation of guided wave can synchronously represent the wave motion state at the weld and the defects. It can also simulate the wave propagation characteristics at the weld. In the simulation, when there is no defect in the weld, the group velocity of SH guided wave is around 2886 m/s, however, defects in the weld will attenuate the guided wave, increase dispersion and slow down group velocity. By comparing the experimental and simulated data, the simulated and experimented results are in good agreement with each other and show that the peridynamics can simulate the SH guided wave at the weld and defects, which provides a theoretical basis for the study of SH guided wave at weld.

articleTitle: Circuit-field coupled analysis of excitation performance of multi-layer spiral coil Electromagnetic Acoustic Transducer
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In the previously finite element and analytical model for the excitation process of electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT), it is generally assumed that the EMAT coil is provided with a current of a limited amplitude. Meanwhile, pulse power amplifier, resistance of transmission line, impedance matching network and coil equivalent impedance are not taken into consideration. In this paper, an excitation equivalent circuit model for the EMAT is established, effects of the output voltage and output impedance of pulse power amplifier, impedance matching parameters and characteristics of the excitation coil on the EMAT conversion efficiency are considered. Based on experiments, influences of connecting mode (series or parallel) of multi-layer coil, coil conductor diameter and number of coil layers on the EMAT efficiency with various frequencies are studied. Results show that for the multi-layer spiral coil EMAT at 1MHz and 2MHz, it is better to use parallel connecting method. The EMAT efficiency is rapidly decreased with the increase of number of coil layer when spiral coils are connected in series. When the EMAT coil is perfectly matched, the output impedance of the pulse generator, resistance of transmission line and the EMAT dynamic coil impedance (number of layers, wire diameter, excitation frequency) also meet special conditions, the EMAT excitation efficiency can be maximized.

articleTitle: Research on Ultrasonic Lamb Wave defect signal recognition method based on VMD
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to extract the defect from ultrasonic lamb wave signal accurately, the method based on variational mode decomposition (VMD) is proposed. The effect of decomposition produces different results due to the change of the decomposition layer - K. If the value of K is too large or too small, the intrinsic mode function (IMF) cannot be completely separated, resulting in mode aliasing phenomenon. The false components produced in the decomposition process will cause the summation of energy of the decomposed components to be larger than the original signal. In order to address this problem, the relationship between the mean of instantaneous frequency and the K value is used to determine the specific decomposition layer number of the VMD. The mutual information value of each IMF component and the original signal is calculated, and the IMF whose mutual information is lower than the threshold value will be eliminated to remove the false component. This method can decompose the fault signal well in the practical non-destructive testing and provide reference for the application of VMD in the faulted diagnosis of non-destructive testing.

articleTitle: Development and Application of spherical Ultrasonic Array probe for 3D Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to obtain high-resolution three-dimensional images using photoacoustic tomography, we fabricated a hemispherical array sensor. It is used to detect signals of various shapes such as blood vessels that propagate in different directions, and the piezoelectric transducers are placed in hemispheres as much as possible to obtain high-resolution three-dimensional images. And the sensor can receive the wide ultrasonic wave from low frequency to high frequency to deal with the change of ultrasonic frequency with the observation object. The hemispherical array sensor developed by piezoelectric element is used to image iron wire and blood vessel. The results show that the sensor can obtain high imaging resolution.

articleTitle: Study on eddy current signal processing algorithms for oxide layer measurement of fuel rods
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Eddy current testing has been widely used in oxide layer measurement of fuel rods. However, the measured signal will be interfered by multiple factors due to the limitation of eddy current techniques. The emphasis of this paper is to eliminate these interference signals. A variety of signal processing algorithms are presented in this paper, with linear fitting algorithm for correcting the signal drift, with grid filtering algorithm and amplitude-limiting filtering algorithm for eliminating the grid signals and other spike signals, with Savitzky-Golay filtering algorithm for smoothing the signal. All the processing algorithms were simulated in MATLAB with a view to demonstrate the feasibility. The simulation results indicate that these algorithms are effective and practical.

articleTitle: Application of Micro-CT and SEM Technology In-situ Observation of Damage Evolution of C/SiC Composites
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to investigate the damage behavior of C/SiC composites, SEM and micro-CT were combined and run with in-situ tensile tests to study the damage phenomenology. The microscopic processes of crack initiation, propagation and failure of C/SiC composites with circular hole were directly observed under tensile load. The results show that the method proposed in this paper can be used to analyze and visualize crack initiation and propagation. The crack propagation of C/SiC composites is diverse when the material fails, and the morphology of the internal cracks observed in the micro- CT images is different from the surface cracks observed in the SEM images. The macroscopic holes of the C/SiC material and the boundary of the SiC matrix aggregate region often become the crack initiation of the specimen, and the main crack which eventually causes the failure of specimen is located in the preset macroscopic hole region. Through the method proposed in this paper, the micro-structure images of the specimen in the elastic deformation stage, micro-crack propagation stage and failure stage can be obtained, which correspond to the characteristics of the linear stage, curve stage and fluctuation stage of the load-displacement curve respectively. The microscopic observation method combined with micro-CT and SEM is important and useful to the study of the failure evolution mechanism of C/SiC composite materials.

articleTitle: Research on microcrack algorithm based on eddy current pulsed thermography
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: With the increase of fatigue rolling cycles between the wheel and rail, it's easy to generate small angle microcracks on the surface or shallow surface of the rail, which is located in the blind spot of ultrasonic detection. Therefore, pulsed eddy current thermography (ECPT) is selected for detection. In this paper, the finite element software was used to simulate the thermal characteristics of microcracks, and the data was extracted for simulation data analysis. Then principal component analysis(PCA), tensor CANDECOMP/PARAFAC de- composition(CP), and Tucker decomposition were compared horizontally, and the signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) of the three algorithms were obtained by experimental data. Experimental analysis shows that the characteristics of microcracks are very weak, the optimal extraction time is in the beginning of the heating stage, and the tensor algorithm can improve the SNR ratio of the microcrack effectively.

articleTitle: An improved predictive deconvolution based on wavelet analysis for GPR signal processing
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to reduce the interference of multiple echoes from water and metal on detection effect of ground penetrating radar (GPR), an improved predictive deconvolution has been proposed based on wavelet analysis (short for PDWA method). The PDWA method firstly decomposes the GPR signals into time domain sub-signals with different scales by wavelet analysis, and then filters the time domain sub-signals by predictive deconvolution and wavelet threshold denoising, at last reconstructs the filtered sub-signals to obtain the analysis result. Processing detection signal of model experiment by the PDWA method, the result shows that, comparing with predictive deconvolution, the PDWA method can suppress multiple echo interference, identify the target reflection accurately, and enhance the signal to interference ratio (SIR) of target reflection, thereby improving the detection resolution and the accuracy of image analysis of GPR signals.

articleTitle: Attention structured Pattern Deep Learning for region induction thermography NDT
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Induction Thermography is a crucial nondestructive testing technology which has a rapidly increasing range of applications for crack detection. A series of studies have been carried out in thermal sequences processing algorithms. However, these methods often suffer from the complex surface conditions of experiment components. In this study, we propose an end-to-end attention structured pattern deep learning method to achieve precise crack detection and localization. The proposed method integrates both time and spatial pattern mining for crack information with a deep region convolution neural network. Experiments on welding line cracks have shown attractive performance and verified the efficacy of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Study on Characteristics of Magnetoacoustic Emission for Q235 Steel Subject to Fatigue Process
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Fatigue fracture is one of the failure modes in the ferromagnetic metal material. The suddenness of the fracture often causes the catastrophic accident Therefore, in order to prevent the fatigue failure of metal materials, the detection and evaluation of the early fatigue state of metal materials are very important. However, the traditional nondestructive testing (NDT) methods are not suitable for the rapid detection of early fatigue conditions of metal materials. Therefore some advanced NDT methods need to be proposed. Magnetoacoustic emission (MAE) is a great potential NDT method in early fatigue testing of ferromagnetic metal materials, because MAE is sensitive to the microstructure and stress state of materials. Therefore, in this paper, the low cycle fatigue of Q235 steel is analyzed by finite element simulation. The life of Q235 steel is also predicted according to Smith-Watson-Topper(SWT) model. Finally, the MAE characteristics of low cycle fatigue in Q235 steel is given.

articleTitle: Phase-Controlled Focusing Method of Ultrasound Guided Wave Based on Synchronous Control of Time Delay and Amplitude Factor
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In the detection of gun barrel defects with ultrasonic guided wave, the echo coefficients are often used to express the influence of defects on the propagation characteristics of guided waves. The echo coefficient is closely related to the size of defects. If the defect in the barrel is small, the defect echo of the guided wave will be submerged in the noise, so that the value of the echo coefficient cannot be obtained by the detection, resulting in missed and false detections. Therefore, in order to improve the accuracy of ultrasonic guided wave detection technology, a phase-controlled focusing detection method of ultrasonic guided wave based on synchronous control of time delay and amplitude factor is proposed through scientific analysis methods such as theoretical analysis, numerical simulation and simulation calculation. This method can improve the signal-to-noise ratio and echo coefficient of the echo signal, enhance the ability to detect small defects in the barrel with the guided wave. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Eddy Current Testing of Surface Cracks on GH4169 Alloy Turbine Disk
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: GH4169 alloy turbine disk is one of the critical components in hot end of the aeroengine. It is prone to cracks, especially surface cracks which can significantly undermine the quality of disk, resulting in fatigue fracture and thereby catastrophic failures. In this paper, eddy current testing (ECT) of surface cracks was investigated through simulations based on CIVA and experiments. The ECT probes in different configurations and parameters were modelled and impedance curves were computed. The parameter and structure of probe was determined by analyzing the signal decay rate and defect resolution. Following this, experimental investigation was carried out to verify the simulation results. It could be found that experimental results matched well with simulation results and the probe designed via simulations was applicable. The related results from both simulations and experiments are supportive of ECT of surface cracks on GH4169 turbine disk.

articleTitle: Determination of hardness in welded rail surface via Barkhausen noise
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: At present, the railway mainly uses eutectoid pearlite rails. The hyper-eutectoid steel improves the strength and hardness of the rail compared to the eutectoid pearlite steel, and is now laid on heavy-duty railway lines. Aiming at the failure of welded rail, welding surface was tested by the magnetic Barkhausen noise (MBN) method. Combined with the surface hardness test and metallographic analysis, hardness changed and structural transformation caused by flash welding was analyzed from the microscopic point of view. The relationship between hardness and MBN signal was quantitatively analyzed, results showed that there was a good correlation between two parameters.

articleTitle: Development and application of high signal-to-noise ratio air-coupled ultrasonic sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: With the large-scale construction of natural gas pipeline, the pressure level has been increasing, even reaching the range of three types of pressure vessels. Once there is an explosion, the damage is enormous. Therefore, higher and higher requirements are put forward for the accuracy and speed of pipeline damage detection. In order to improve the detection accuracy and speed of pipeline, a method of ultrasonic ring guided wave detection with air coupling excitation is proposed. In order to facilitate the realization of intelligent internal detection of gas pipelines, we designed an optimized linear focusing high-sensitivity air coupling sensor, studied it from both numerical simulation and experiment, and designed an internal detection system of gas pipelines, providing a theoretical basis for the development of ultrasonic internal detection technology of gas pipelines. The results show that the signal-to-noise ratio of the optimized linear focusing air-coupled ultrasonic sensor is improved.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic time reversal based imaging for extended target
publicationTitle: 2019 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, the time reversal based imaging methods have been used in the area of ultrasonic Non-destructive evaluation (NDE) for extended target, the size of which is on the order of the ultrasonic wavelength or larger. Both time reversal with multiple signal classification (TR-MUSIC) and phase-coherent multiple signal classification (PC-MUSIC), the two typical time reversal based imaging methods, have been introduced to obtain the ultrasonic image by post-processing the pulse-echo signals belonging to the ultrasonic array data. Experimental system has been designed and built to capture the real ultrasonic array data via full matrix capture (FMC) process from the test sample. The experiment was implemented on a block of Al with Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) line, which can be considered as the extended target. The experimental results show that PC-MUSIC over the given frequency range can provide the shape and size of the extended target, however, TR-MUSIC fails. In addition, the various dimensions of signal subspace are chosen, and its effect on the imaging result has been studied.
